why: the presenter at her desk, level and unhurried; the word hurry sets beside her as she says it, then the frame slides past her into an ordinary office at the end of the day
a drawn office at dusk, one figure at a laptop; a new message slides into the inbox and the camera pushes in until the message fills the screen, its subject line and deadline readable
the cursor drifts across the message and settles on the link; everything freezes mid-motion and the frame holds still for a beat of silence
the frozen message stays dimmed behind; three short anchors set one by one in the open space beside it
the frozen message shrinks back into a full, ordinary inbox; a long imagined list of tips fans out and folds away, leaving one empty frame for four items
the word phishing set large over the dimmed message; three small marks appear on the message itself as each aim is named: the link, the password box, a payment line
the four moves in large plain type, set one by one over the dimmed frozen message, which never leaves the frame
moves three and four join the first two; the fourth sits a little apart, with a quiet mark of emphasis
the four moves slide aside, move three stays lit; an empty funnel draws in, with a small office block at its mouth labelled as one company
a counter at the top of the funnel reads 1,800 as the emails pour in; the filter layer catches them and the counter drains to 50 as 1,750 fall away; the 50 land as small envelopes in a row of inboxes
among the 50 envelopes, 25 small report marks light up one after another; a few of them carry a small click mark first
the 25 lights travel back up out of the inboxes to the security team's desk, arriving before anything else signals the problem
the security desk lights up and a calm ring spreads out from it across the other inboxes in the building
the funnel shrinks to a small icon in the corner and the frozen message from the opening returns to centre
the camera pushes back into Jo's message; a magnifier passes over it looking for typos and finds none, each line ticks clean
the magnifier sets down; a plain label beside the message reads spelling, not reliable, and the message stays clean and convincing
the message held still; the deadline line lifts off it as a marked callout labelled pressure, and stays pinned on the board beside the message
the sender name lifts off as a second callout, authority, pinned under pressure; the two together form the pressure family
the camera closes on the address; the real spelling slides in beneath it and the one changed letter lights up, everything else grey
the short link unfolds into its full destination, which is plainly not the shared drive; it lifts off as a callout and joins the address under the label mismatch
the password box lifts off as the last callout, request; Jo's inbox has now become an evidence board with three families pinned around one clean message
the three family labels brighten in turn on the evidence board, then the message dims and the two moves set over it
the evidence board slides away and a new message arrives in the same inbox, from a familiar contact with a known avatar
the supplier message held on screen, its name and logo familiar, the attachment icon at the bottom, nothing marked yet
the familiar name glows softly; the rest of the message waits unmarked while the viewer looks
the three signs mark themselves on the supplier message in the order spoken: the word today, the bank details, the attachment
beside the message, a separate path draws out to the supplier's contact found in the company's own records, bypassing the link and number in the message
the supplier email re-forms as a phone text, then as a chat bubble, side by side; the same three sign marks line up across all three while only the channel changes
a small, quiet label sits under the text and chat bubbles: in simulations, 40% higher than email; no headline, no alarm
the three channels settle into one row and a single report mark lands on each
a brief glimpse of the funnel with its 25 lights, then a slow dip to a new time and a different desk
a second drawn figure between meetings, laptop half open; a delivery notice, a click, and the screen carries on as if nothing changed
Ravi pauses with a small thought bubble holding the tempting line; the frame stays soft and unhurried
from the click the frame splits in two; on the left path the message is deleted and the early-warning light from the funnel flickers at Ravi's desk and never travels to the security team
on the right path a report goes out, the light travels to the security desk and arrives, and Ravi's screen settles into a calm handled state
the split resolves to the right-hand path only; Ravi back at his desk, the day carrying on, nothing dramatic
move four from the opening list returns, large and plain, over Ravi's settled desk
a fresh chat message on screen, the question above and four option cards as peers below it, then a real silent pause
card C lifts and the two signs mark themselves on the chat message; then B and D each get one plain line on why they fall short, while A stays grey
the opening dusk office and Jo's frozen message return; the four signs mark themselves on it in quick succession, then the frame holds for the viewer to answer
the cursor moves off the link to the report control; the message folds away into a calm handled state and the office settles, no celebration
the presenter returns, level and dry; the pocket rule sets beside her in two lines
